source_evidence.observation: The source states the one-way qualitative claim that any sub-gaussian distribution is sub-exponential.
Sub-gaussianity is defined by the equivalent properties i--iv, and the psi_2 norm is inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}.
Sub-exponentiality is defined by the equivalent properties a--d, and the psi_1 norm is inf {t > 0 : E exp(|X|/t) <= 2}.

binders: X, a real-valued random variable (equivalently, its distribution)
hypotheses: X is sub-gaussian in the sense of Definition 2.5.6.
conclusions: X is sub-exponential in the sense of Definition 2.7.5.
definitions_and_conventions: Definition 2.5.6: X is sub-gaussian when it satisfies one of the equivalent properties i--iv of Proposition 2.5.2.
The sub-gaussian norm is ||X||_{psi_2} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}.
Definition 2.7.5: X is sub-exponential when it satisfies one of the equivalent properties a--d of Proposition 2.7.1.
The sub-exponential norm is ||X||_{psi_1} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(|X|/t) <= 2}.
implicit_context: Expectations and probabilities are with respect to the underlying probability distribution of X.
The implication is qualitative; the cited body sentence does not state a numerical psi_1-versus-psi_2 norm bound.

details: The claim runs from sub-gaussian to sub-exponential, not conversely.
The conclusion places every sub-gaussian law in the larger class having at least exponential tail decay.

undebatable_constraints: The premise must be sub-gaussianity and the conclusion must be sub-exponentiality.
No centering, independence, or pairing with another random variable appears in this source claim.
No explicit quantitative comparison between ||X||_{psi_1} and ||X||_{psi_2} is part of the cited sentence.
The meanings of sub-gaussian and sub-exponential must be compatible with Definitions 2.5.6 and 2.7.5, including displays (2.13) and (2.21).
contracts.contract_plain_english: For every real random variable X, if X is sub-gaussian according to the book's Section 2.5 definition, then X is sub-exponential according to the Section 2.7 definition. The cited sentence asserts only this qualitative inclusion and gives no explicit norm constant.
